Maintenance Report — MNT-0087-003

Asset: WELL-0087 (SW-24 Well 087, T200, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: downhole pump Work started: 04 Mar 2023 08:00 · Finished: 06 Mar 2023 23:00 · Well stopped for this job: 63 hours Crew lead: Megan Ward (U-305) · Crew: Kevin Price · Contractor: Sandstone Rod & Pump Triggered by: inspection INS-0087-0018 on 2023-03-02 Report written: 07 Mar 2023

What happened

Field staff reported that fluid stopped reaching the flowline and the rod load spiked on the downstroke. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0087-0018 showed the wellhead at 11.4 °C with the air at 9.1 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The downhole pump was stuck, most likely from sand or scale.

Root cause

A worn plunger that let sand settle and lock the pump.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 2 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Rigged up the company workover rig on the well.
  2. Pulled the rods and the insert pump.
  3. Inspected the pump: sand in the barrel and a worn plunger.
  4. Ran in a new insert pump.
  5. Re-spaced the pump and hung the rods back on.

Summary of the fix: pulled and replaced downhole pump.

Testing and return to service

Pump test confirmed fluid to surface and the wellhead warmed back to normal. The well was returned to production.

Maintenance Report — MNT-0087-004

Asset: WELL-0087 (SW-24 Well 087, T200, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: flowline Work started: 21 Apr 2023 08:00 · Finished: 21 Apr 2023 23:00 · Well stopped for this job: 15 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Megan Ward Triggered by: inspection INS-0087-0025 on 2023-04-20 Report written: 22 Apr 2023

What happened

The weekly drone inspection INS-0087-0025 at 07:30 on 2023-04-20 found crude oil on the pad: about 5.4% of the pad area, estimated 1.4 bbl. The inspector noted: "Oil sheen around cellar." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 2.6 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to the flanged flowline connection at the wellhead cellar.

Root cause

A failed gasket on the flange where the flowline leaves the wellhead.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Cleaned free oil out of the cellar.
  2. Unbolted the flange and removed the failed gasket.
  3. Fitted a new gasket and new bolts, torqued to specification.
  4. Excavated the stained soil around the cellar.

Summary of the fix: replaced the flange gasket and bolts and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 200 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 160 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste

  • About 1.9 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0087-004 (WS-06).
  • 2 soil samples taken around the spill; the highest result after clean-up was 0.39% TPH, below the 1.0% target (SR-03).

Maintenance Report — MNT-0087-010

Asset: WELL-0087 (SW-24 Well 087, T200, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: flowline Work started: 10 May 2024 08:00 · Finished: 11 May 2024 09:00 · Well stopped for this job: 25 hours Crew lead: Kevin Price (U-303) · Crew: Brian Coleman, Megan Ward Triggered by: inspection INS-0087-0080 on 2024-05-09 Report written: 13 May 2024

What happened

The weekly manual inspection INS-0087-0080 at 07:15 on 2024-05-09 found crude oil on the pad: about 7.1% of the pad area, estimated 1.5 bbl. The inspector noted: "Pooled fluid near flowline." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 3.4 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to a threaded coupling on the flowline close to the wellhead.

Root cause

Corrosion under a failed protective wrap on the coupling.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 0% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the coupling.
  2. Cut out the failed coupling and the pipe ends.
  3. Welded in new pipe and a new fitting.
  4. Coated the new joints.
  5. Excavated the stained soil.
  6. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: replaced leaking flowline section and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 200 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 160 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste

  • About 2.5 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0087-010 (WS-06).
  • 2 soil samples taken around the spill; the highest result after clean-up was 0.66% TPH, below the 1.0% target (SR-03).
